arches-delicate-arch.name: Delicate Arch
arches-delicate-arch.blurb: Red sandstone, open slickrock and one famous span. Delicate Arch stands on its own at the rim of a stone bowl in Arches National Park, near Moab, reached by a roughly three-mile round-trip hike across bare rock. At sunset the whole arch glows orange.
arches-delicate-arch.spot: Delicate Arch, Arches National Park, near Moab, Utah

crater-lake-wizard-island.name: Wizard Island
crater-lake-wizard-island.blurb: Deep blue water inside a sleeping volcano. Crater Lake fills the caldera of Mount Mazama in southern Oregon, and at 1,943 feet it's the deepest lake in the United States. Wizard Island, a cinder cone, rises from the water near its western shore.
crater-lake-wizard-island.spot: Wizard Island, Crater Lake National Park, Oregon

grand-canyon-yaki-point.name: Yaki Point
grand-canyon-yaki-point.blurb: Layered cliffs, red rock and a mile of open air. Yaki Point juts out from the South Rim of Grand Canyon National Park, just east of Grand Canyon Village, near the start of the South Kaibab Trail. The canyon opens wide in almost every direction.
grand-canyon-yaki-point.spot: Yaki Point, South Rim, Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona

grand-teton-schwabacher-landing.name: Schwabacher Landing
grand-teton-schwabacher-landing.blurb: Still water, beaver ponds and jagged peaks. Schwabacher Landing sits beside the Snake River in Grand Teton National Park, where quiet side channels hold a mirror image of the Teton Range at sunrise. It's one of the park's best-loved views.
grand-teton-schwabacher-landing.spot: Schwabacher Landing, Snake River, Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming

lake-tahoe-emerald-bay.name: Emerald Bay
lake-tahoe-emerald-bay.blurb: Clear water, granite shores and one small island. Emerald Bay tucks into the southwest corner of Lake Tahoe, home to Fannette Island, the only island in the lake, and Vikingsholm, a 1920s Scandinavian-style mansion on the shore. The water shifts from green to deep blue.
lake-tahoe-emerald-bay.spot: Emerald Bay State Park, Lake Tahoe, California

yellowstone-grand-prismatic-spring.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
yellowstone-grand-prismatic-spring.blurb: Rings of blue, gold and orange under drifting steam. Grand Prismatic Spring in Yellowstone's Midway Geyser Basin is the largest hot spring in the United States, about 370 feet across, its colors made by heat-loving microbes. It's best seen from the hillside above.
yellowstone-grand-prismatic-spring.spot: Grand Prismatic Spring, Midway Geyser Basin, Yellowstone National Park, Wyoming

yosemite-half-dome.name: Half Dome
yosemite-half-dome.blurb: Sheer granite above a valley of pines. Half Dome rises more than 4,700 feet above Yosemite Valley in California's Sierra Nevada, its flat northwest face catching the last light of the day. Hikers reach the top by a pair of cables up its rounded back.
yosemite-half-dome.spot: Half Dome, Yosemite Valley, Yosemite National Park, California

zion-angels-landing.name: Angels Landing
zion-angels-landing.blurb: Red cliffs, a narrow fin of rock and the Virgin River far below. Angels Landing rises about 1,500 feet above Zion Canyon, and the last stretch to the top follows a chain-lined spine with sheer drops on both sides. A permit is required for the chains.
zion-angels-landing.spot: Angels Landing, Zion Canyon, Zion National Park, Utah
